question.:question/problem: Find $t$ given that the vectors $p=⟨3,t,t⟩$, $q=⟨1,3,1⟩$, and $r=⟨1,1,3⟩$ are coplanar.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Computing the triple product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot (q\times r) & =|\begin{aligned}3 & t & t \\ 1 & 3 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =3\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}|-t\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}|+t\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =3(3\cdot 3-1\cdot 1)-t(1\cdot 3-1\cdot 1)+t(1\cdot 1-3\cdot 1) \\  & =24-2t-2t \\  & =24-4t.\end{aligned}
$$

    

Three vectors are coplanar if and only if their triple product is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot (q\times r) & =0 \\ 24-4t & =0 \\ t & =6\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the three vectors are coplanar if and only if $t=6.$

question.:question/problem: Find $k$ given that the vectors $a=⟨k,1,4⟩,$ $b=⟨8,0,3⟩,$ and $c=⟨3,1,1⟩$ are coplanar.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Computing the triple product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =|\begin{aligned}k & 1 & 4 \\ 8 & 0 & 3 \\ 3 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =k\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|-1\cdot |\begin{aligned}8 & 3 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}|+4\cdot |\begin{aligned}8 & 0 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =k(0\cdot 1-1\cdot 3)-(8\cdot 1-3\cdot 3)+4(8\cdot 1-3\cdot 0) \\  & =-3k+1+32 \\  & =33-3k \\  & =3(11-k).\end{aligned}
$$

    

Three vectors are coplanar if and only if their triple product is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =0 \\ 3(11-k) & =0 \\ 11-k & =0 \\ k & =11\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the three vectors are coplanar if and only if $k=11.$

question.:question/problem: Find $t$ given that the vectors $p=⟨t,t,1⟩,$ $q=⟨3,2,6⟩,$ and $r=⟨3,4,0⟩$ are coplanar.

Computing the triple product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot (q\times r) & =|\begin{aligned}t & t & 1 \\ 3 & 2 & 6 \\ 3 & 4 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =t\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & 6 \\ 4 & 0\end{aligned}|-t\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 6 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}|+1\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =t(2\cdot 0-4\cdot 6)-t(3\cdot 0-3\cdot 6)+(3\cdot 4-3\cdot 2) \\  & =-24t+18t+6 \\  & =-6t+6 \\  & =6(1-t).\end{aligned}
$$

    

Three vectors are coplanar if and only if their triple product is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot (q\times r) & =0 \\ 6(1-t) & =0 \\ 1-t & =0 \\ t & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the three vectors are coplanar if and only if $t=1.$

\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =0 \\ 5-k & =0 \\ k & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the three vectors are coplanar if and only if $k=5.$

knowledge_point.title: Determining Whether Three Vectors are Coplanar

question.:question/problem:
Find $k$ given that the vectors $x=⟨1,k,2⟩$, $y=⟨5,-2,3⟩$, and $z=⟨-4,k,1⟩$ are coplanar.

$k=${{field-1}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Computing the triple product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x\cdot (y\times z) & =|\begin{aligned}1 & k & 2 \\ 5 & -2 & 3 \\ -4 & k & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot |\begin{aligned}-2 & 3 \\ k & 1\end{aligned}|-k\cdot |\begin{aligned}5 & 3 \\ -4 & 1\end{aligned}|+2\cdot |\begin{aligned}5 & -2 \\ -4 & k\end{aligned}| \\  & =1(-2\cdot 1-3\cdot k)-k(5\cdot 1-3\cdot -4)+2(5k-(-2)(-4)) \\  & =-2-3k-k(5+12)+2(5k-8) \\  & =-2-3k-17k+10k-16 \\  & =-10k-18\end{aligned}
$$

Three vectors are coplanar if and only if their triple product is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}x\cdot (y\times z) & =0 \\ -10k-18 & =0 \\ k & =-\frac{9}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the three vectors are coplanar if and only if $k=-\frac{9}{5}.$
